synopsis: The booklet recommends evidence-based stage gates for governance within a layered planning architecture, not as a complete planning method; four or five evidence gates are suggested, while causal evidence for Stage-Gate in highly uncertain, safety-critical virtual validation was not found [f203, f9492, f9510, f9507, f9589]. South African mining provides a staged-verification precedent: the MOSH regime dated 11 October 2025 establishes TRL4 and TRL7 gates, a surface CPS TRL7 specification is dated 20 January 2026, and independent verification is required at both gates [f15563, f557, f2459]. Gate decisions should permit go, restricted continuation, pivot and stop under pre-committed criteria signed by the sponsor and a named decider; launch should depend on unresolved safety evidence rather than calendar pressure [f9449, f10708]. Funding should be tied to early experiments, with explicit stop or escalation triggers for unusable supplier data, missing evidence ownership, and physical-versus-virtual discrepancies that undermine the safety conclusion [f10746, f10918, f10924, f10933]. The eleven-month planning window motivates small parallel options selected at the first gate, and the illustrative cadence ends April 2027 with an independent delivery-readiness decision of ready, restricted scope or fallback [f9594, f9655]. Important limitations remain: public literature cannot establish whether the architecture meets company safety-release criteria, rigid gates can become date-driven ceremonies, and pilot-methodology support for pre-declared progression criteria is analogical rather than direct proof [f4975, f9506, f9487].

relations.note: Both identify the South African surface TRL7 specification dated 20 January 2026.
Both justify pre-committed stop and descope criteria using escalation-of-commitment literature.
Both tie launch to unresolved safety evidence rather than calendar pressure.
Both require independent verification at MOSH TRL4 and TRL7 gates.
Both identify divergent simulated and real sensor degradation as a stop signal.
The dated Requirements Verification Regime identifies the source of the TRL4 and TRL7 gates.
Specific independent-verification requirements detail the broader shift away from supplier claims.
Adds the TRL4 acceptance criterion to the independent-verification requirement.
No single complete method supports layering complementary planning approaches.
Specifies evidence-based stage gates as the governance component of the layered architecture.
Ceremonial date-driven gates explain why pass criteria should require evidence.
Evidence of escalating commitment supports pre-committed stop and descope criteria.
Adds restricted continuation, stop, signed criteria and named decision ownership to pivot permission.
April 2027 rehearsal illustrates an independent gate with readiness, restriction and fallback outcomes.
Physical-versus-virtual correlation supplies a concrete early experiment and stopping criterion.
Dry-run stopping criteria test whether required evidence has a plan and owner.
Receiving assessor feedback by gate two depends on sufficiently early assessor engagement.
Aggregate-only release feedback operationalizes separation of tuning and release-evidence streams.
